facts.text: The Crucible was a primordial convergence of all living things, described in item descriptions as the source from which all life in the Lands Between originally came, an age when life was not divided into species or hierarchies but existed in chaotic communion, with traits like tails, wings, and carapaces expressing freely.
An older tree called the Great Tree existed at the center of the Crucible age, predating the current Erdtree, referenced in items like the Root Resin and the Crucible Knight armor set.
Ancient dragons existed before the Golden Order and may have had their own prior cosmic order and god predating the Greater Will.
A distant cosmic presence called the Greater Will sent a daughter, Marika, and a golden being called the Elden Beast toward the Lands Between.
The current Erdtree grew around the Elden Ring, absorbing and subsuming the older Great Tree that existed before it.
The Golden Order reached an accommodation with some ancient dragons rather than conquering all of them outright, as evidenced by dragon communion rituals involving consuming dragon hearts.
An incantation description states that everything was originally in opposition to the tree, but through countless victories in war it became the embodiment of order.
Murals from the Golden Order's early era, called the Age of Plenty, depict the Erdtree standing straight and tall, unlike its leaning posture in the game's present.
Before the Erdtree, the horns of an Omen signified divinity, but after the Golden Order's establishment, Omens were seen as cursed beings without grace, having their horns cut off and being enslaved.

The Elden Ring itself is described as the fundamental law of the world given physical shape as a ring, with every boss existing in relationship to its breaking and the wars that followed the Shattering.
Traces of the Rune of Death spread through the Erdtree's root network, appearing as Death Root.
The spread of the Rune of Death created a new category of beings called 'those who live in death,' undead people who cannot properly return to the Erdtree.
Every demigod touched by a Great Rune's concentrated power was driven toward madness.
The Tarnished's journey leads through demigods, ruins, underground cities, and frozen mountaintops before reaching Leyndell, the royal capital.
Astel's presence is connected to the Nox people and the cosmic catastrophe that created the Lake of Rot.
The Frenzied Flame is an outer god representing dissolution, seeking to end individual separation and return all things to undifferentiated unity.
The Land of Shadow is where Marika originated, before her ascension to godhood.

The Shadow of the Erdtree DLC expands the game's bosses to explore what the Golden Order's divine structure was built upon, what it cost, and what persists in the hidden realm where those costs were paid.

The Erdtree in the game's present cannot be entered, its golden bark sealed over by thorns that no conventional weapon can break; sorcerers claim it is withered while priests claim it is merely dormant awaiting a new Elden Lord.
The Realm of Shadow contains the Gate of Divinity, the same gate Marika used to become a god.
The game identifies at least half a dozen Outer Gods clearly, with hints of others whose names remain obscure.
The God of Scarlet Rot is an ancient deity that was defeated and sealed beneath the lakes, in what became the Lake of Rot.
The Formless Mother, also called the Mother of Truth, is the Outer God that Mohg worships, associated with burning blood, wounds, and brutal intimacy.
The Fell God is depicted as a malformed one-eyed deity with curled horns and braided red hair, associated with primordial fire preceding the Erdtree's golden warmth.
The Frenzied Flame is delivered through the Three Fingers, said to be a counterpart to the Greater Will's Two Fingers, once part of a single whole.
The Dark Moon, Ranni's chosen Outer God, is cold, silver, and distant, governing fate, stars, and the unknown, offering freedom rather than commandment.
The ruins of Limgrave suggest a civilization that was once whole.
The Academy of Raya Lucaria represents a tradition of magical scholarship that persisted stubbornly even as the world fell apart.
The Mountaintops of the Giants reflect a genocide carried out in the name of order.

The player character is called Tarnished, once blessed with the grace of the Erdtree, who lost it and was exiled from the Lands Between, then died and was called back by a new Grace toward the Erdtree to seek the Elden Lordship.
The Lands Between is ruled by Queen Marika the Eternal, and the Elden Ring is the source of the Erdtree.
Demigods are described as warped Lords who began as members of a royal and noble family, ruling their domains with power granted by shards of the Elden Ring.
Those blessed by the Elden Ring and Erdtree are marked by a golden aura visible in their eyes; those who lost their grace were exiled and labeled the Tarnished.

The Lands Between is divided into seven distinct areas, each overseen by a Demigod: Limgrave, Caelid, Liurnia of the Lakes, Altus Plateau, Mt. Gelmir, Mountaintops of the Giants, and underground river locations.
If an Empyrean defies the will of the Two Fingers, their Shadow is fated to go mad and oppose them.

The Shadow of the Erdtree DLC takes players to the Realm of Shadow, a dark, death-filled counterpart of the Lands Between hidden beneath a shrouded cloud south of the Erdtree, featuring the Scadutree, a shadowy counterpart to the Erdtree.
The DLC's story centers on the ambitions of Miquella, Messmer, and St. Trina, and explores the history of the Hornsent faction.
The Nox were punished for a rebellion against the Greater Will, their cities forced underground as a form of exile.
The Scadutree Avatar's guardianship predates the current age, dating to a time before the Erdtree dominated, when the Shadow Tree's realm was simply the world rather than a hidden counterpart.
The Fell God is the ancient fire deity of the giants that Marika and Godfrey went to war against in the early days of the Golden Order.
The ancient people of Mt. Gelmir worshipped a powerful serpent god, offering it sacrifices.

Marika directed Godfrey to wage war against the Fire Giants because their flame of ruin threatened the Erdtree; this campaign, the defining war of the early Golden Order, nearly annihilated the giants entirely.

Godfrey fought and made peace with some ancient dragons, defeated the Storm Lord in single combat (an event still echoed in Stormveil Castle's architecture), and led wars expanding the Golden Order's influence, including against the Fire Giants.
One Fire Giant was deliberately spared and cursed/chained at the Mountaintops of the Giants to keep a forge flame—too strong for Marika to extinguish—burning for future use in opening the Erdtree.
When Godfrey destroyed nearly all the giants, the Fell God lost most of its followers but did not die, and still lurks in the Mountaintops of the Giants.
Rennala's mastery of lunar magic allowed her to become head of the Academy of Raya Lucaria and its Glintstone Knights, and to establish the Carian family as royalty.

After the war against the Fire Giants ended with no worthy opponents remaining, Marika deliberately stripped Godfrey and his warriors/kinfolk of their grace, exiling them beyond the Lands Between (across the Sea of Fog to the Badlands, in what became known as the Long March), commanding them to become the first Tarnished and wage war.
Marika promised the exiled Tarnished that after death she would eventually return their grace and give them a chance to return and serve as Elden Lord.

The people of the eternal cities (sometimes called the 'Dox' people) were once the most advanced scholars of the Lands Between, studying stars and cosmic forces and building underground cities lit by artificial constellations, before being punished for rebelling against the Greater Will by having their entire civilization buried underground.
Godfrey was the first human Marika chose as her consort and the warrior who led the campaigns expanding the Erdtree's dominion across the Lands Between.
Radagon's previous marriage to Renala, Queen of the Full Moon of the Carian royal family, was a political alliance between the Golden Order and the Carian sorcerers.
The Finger-Slayer Blade was made in Nokron by a people who had rebelled against the Greater Will and were punished for it.
As chieftain of the badlands, Hoarah Loux was a fierce warrior with strong bloodlust before being selected as Marika's consort.
As an Empyrean, Queen Marika was given Maliketh as a Shadow and half-brother, to whom she entrusted the Rune of Death when the Golden Order was established.
Queen Marika's first consort was Godfrey, with whom she had three children: Godwyn the Golden and the Omen twins Morgott and Mohg.
Royal-blooded Omens, including Morgott and Mohg, were hidden from the world and shackled in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds beneath Leyndell.

On behalf of the Greater Will, Marika and her followers waged wars to spread the Golden Order's influence, most notably against the Storm Lord, the fire giants and their god the One-Eyed God, and the Academy of Raya Lucaria and Carian royal family.
It is unclear which side instigated the wars against the Dragons and against the Godskin Apostles and their god, the Gloam-Eyed Queen.
During Godfrey's reign, gladiatorial combat in colosseums across the Lands Between was common as rituals honoring the Erdtree, a practice that ended when Radagon became Marika's consort.
Marika summoned Radagon back to the Erdtree capital to become her second Elden Lord consort, ending his marriage to Renala, and together they had the twins Miquella and Malenia.
Kale's nomadic clan, the Great Caravan, was accused of heresy and buried alive underground, where they summoned the flame of frenzy.
Marika tasked Radagon with leading the Erdtree's armies in the war against Liurnia of the Lakes.
Sword monuments in Liurnia suggest there were two Liurnian Wars, and during or after the second, Radagon and Rennala met in battle and fell in love.
Godfrey's axe was broken in battle during the Long March, and after the journey he reverted to being a simple warrior while still carrying Serosh on his back.
Radagon sought absolution at the Church of Vows using Celestial Dew, and he and Rennala were married there, uniting Leyndell and the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
Radagon and Rennala had three children together: General Radahn, Praetor Rykard, and Lunar Princess Ranni.
Radagon gifted Rennala an Amber Egg and left her to rejoin Marika's side when Godfrey and his fellow Tarnished were exiled.
When Godfrey was exiled and Radagon returned to Marika's side, Rennala was devastated and grew weak, losing her charm over the Academy.
The Academy's scholars rebelled against the Carian royal family, with the Cuckoo Knights attacking Caria Manor and locking Rennala in the Grand Library.
The opening narration states that on a night of wintry fog, the Rune of Death was stolen and the demigods began to fall, starting with Godwyn the Golden.

Ranni the Witch rejected her fate of being controlled by the Two Fingers and masterminded the Night of the Black Knives, stealing a fragment of the Rune of Death from Maliketh and forging/imbuing it into the Black Knife Assassins' blades.
On the Night of the Black Knives, assassins killed Godwyn the Golden using a fragment of the stolen Rune of Death, carving a death curse mark intended to fully erase both body and soul.

At the exact moment Godwyn died, Ranni took her own life at the top of a high, isolated tower, splitting the death curse mark into two half-circles instead of one complete circle—one half carved into Godwyn's flesh, the other half carried by Ranni's discarded body.
Shabriri was also the name of a man punished for slander by having his eyes gouged out, after which his eyes filled with the flame of frenzy.
According to the Howl of Shabriri, this was the first instance of the maddening sickness of frenzy in the Lands Between.
One night, Rennala took her daughter Ranni out stargazing as she had done in her own childhood, which led to Ranni meeting her own moon, the Dark Moon.

Messmer the Impaler was tasked with purging the tower-dwelling Hornsent, known as Omens in the Lands Between and representing an older religion predating Marika's rule, and he and his forces decimated their people.
The Black Knife Assassins are the Numen women who carried out the Night of the Black Knives, which killed Godwyn, after being subverted by Ranni.
Tanith worked as a dancer in an unnamed foreign land until she caught Rykard's eye and became his consort, and he brought her back to the Lands Between.

Guardians protecting the passage to the deep root depths, and through it Godwyn's resting place, stand between the ordinary world and the aftermath of the Night of the Black Knives, the event in which Godwyn was killed.
The knife that killed Godwyn only carried a fragment of the Rune of Death, so it killed only his soul, leaving his body alive but soulless.
Ranni's body died but her soul survived because she had planned for this outcome in advance.
Ranni transferred her soul into a small doll modeled after a mentor she had loved and lost—the Snow Witch Renna—then vanished from the world's awareness.
To escape the Two Fingers' control, Ranni needed to die in the flesh while preserving her soul, which the Knight of the Black Knives' stolen Rune of Death made possible.
Godwyn's death was the first death of a demigod in the history of the Lands Between.
Ranni, Marika's stepdaughter, used a piece of Marika's own system to murder Marika's firstborn son Godwyn.

When Mohg stood before (or encountered while imprisoned) the Formless Mother, an outer god, his cursed/crucible-marked blood caught fire, and the deity chose him as her vessel, granting him bloodflame incantations.
Marika ordered Maliketh to lock away the Rune of Death, also called Destined Death.
Godwyn's soulless body grew and festered within the underground roots beneath Leyndell, becoming the entity known as the Prince of Death.
Godwyn the Golden's death was the most devastating loss to Marika from the coordinated assassinations, since he embodied everything she hoped the Golden Order could produce.
Rykard encountered the God-Devouring Serpent and offered himself and his Great Rune as sacrifices to gain immortality, allowing him to grow and devour people and gods for eternity.

Following Godwyn's death, Marika took the Elden Ring and shattered it, breaking the fundamental laws of reality and resulting in her own imprisonment within the Erdtree, which triggered the war among the demigods known as the Shattering.
The shards of the shattered Elden Ring flew outward and settled in or near Marika's demigod children, becoming corrupting Great Runes whose power triggered the war known as the Shattering.
Rykard's fall into greed and gluttony caused most of his followers to turn against him, with Tanith remaining a notable exception.

During the Battle of Aeonia, Malenia's needle broke—whether by accident or choice remains ambiguous—unleashing the scarlet rot she had suppressed since birth as the Scarlet Bloom (Scarlet Aeonia), a massive crimson flower that destroyed Caelid, transforming it into a permanent blood-red rotted wasteland.
Radahn halted the stars specifically to prevent Ranni's planned Age of Stars from occurring, since her destiny required the stars to fall.
Malenia marched her army from the Haligtree south to fight Radahn in the Battle of Aeonia, the defining conflict of the Shattering.
Malenia's Cleanrot Knights, who accepted exposure to scarlet rot out of loyalty, fought Radahn's soldiers in one of the bloodiest battles in Lands Between history.
Malenia and Radahn were evenly matched in personal combat, as neither had ever lost a battle before.
After the battle, Malenia fell into a deep, dreamless coma.

Former Gelmir Knights sought out the great spear Serpent-Hunter, designed to kill the immortal God-Devouring Serpent, to stop Rykard, but were unsuccessful, as evidenced by corpses found holding the weapon in his boss room.
A Cleanrot Knight named Finlay carried Malenia's unconscious body alone back to the Haligtree, fighting off enemies the entire way.
After the Shattering ended with no victor, the demigods retreated to their strongholds and Leyndell remained mostly intact but without a true Elden Lord.
Miquella grew the Haligtree from a sapling, watering it with his own Empyrean blood hoping his growth would be reflected in the tree, but it never became a full Erdtree.
While Malenia was fighting Radahn, Mohg, Lord of Blood, kidnapped the sleeping Miquella and took him to his hidden palace underground.

Mohg wrapped Miquella in a cocoon of golden silk and fed him blood in a ritual meant to elevate Miquella to divine status, trying to rouse him with offerings and shared bedchambers, though Miquella never woke.
Through symbolic death in Mohg's cocoon, Miquella broke free of the Erdtree's death-rebirth cycle and shed his flesh piece by piece on his path to the Gate of Divinity.
Messmer was sent to the Land of Shadow to wage a campaign of conquest and was then forgotten, his name removed from records.
Malenia sleeps in the depths of Elphael, the branch of the Haligtree, waiting for Miquella to return.
Even during Malenia's sleep, the scarlet rot she carries continues to spread and corrupt the Haligtree, which Miquella intended as a pure sanctuary.
On a night of wintry fog, a group of unknown assassins struck across the Lands Between, killing many of Queen Marika's kin.
To prevent the Rune of Death from being stolen again, Maliketh bound his sword, imbued with the rune, within his own body and changed his name.
The Shattering was a devastating war between the demigod children of Queen Marika, sparked when the shattering of the Elden Ring caused open war among them, breaking the empire into fragments.
The Shattering meant abandonment of the Lands Between by the Greater Will.
After Malenia's Scarlet Aeonia bloomed in Caelid during the Shattering, Gowry dedicated his services to her, believing she would found a new Order of Rot.
General Radahn recruited Jerren into his army as a guest commander during the Shattering, before he could fulfill his promise to slay Sellen.
Mohg eventually escaped the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and established Mohgwyn Palace in a secluded part of the Siofra River.

No single faction in the Shattering could achieve decisive victory even when empowered by a Great Rune; the battle between General Radahn and Malenia the Severed, which had no victor, demonstrated that neither could conquer all the lands united by Marika, and the Lands Between settled into an unresolved stalemate rather than open war.
Marika's shattering of the Elden Ring is portrayed as a deliberate act by a god who no longer believed in the system she built, not an accident or madness.
Despite being the same person, Marika and Radagon held different wills; when Marika shattered the Elden Ring, Radagon used the same hammer to try to repair it.
During the Shattering, when Leyndell was leaderless, Morgott secretly ruled the capital as the Unveiled Monarch, knowing it wouldn't accept an Omen as leader.
Radahn's mind was destroyed by scarlet rot infection after Malenia released the Scarlet Bloom during the Battle of Aeonia.
During the Second Defense of Leyndell, Morgott successfully defended the capital and the Erdtree from invading demigods.
Vyke took the Frenzied Flame into himself to save his finger maiden from being sacrificed to burn open the Erdtree.
Vyke became a Lord of Frenzy and lost his path to the throne, wandering into madness.
Radahn's loyal soldiers organized the Radahn Festival, inviting warriors worldwide to give their general an honorable death in battle rather than kill him for conquest.
Miquella later attempted to use the same Gate of Divinity at Anor Ilim to claim his own godhood, as depicted in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.
When Radahn was defeated at the Radahn Festival, the stars he held moved and a fragment struck the earth, opening the previously inaccessible underground city of Nokron.
Nokron's opening was specifically what Ranni needed for the next stage of her plan.
Ranni seeks the Finger-Slayer Blade, hidden in the underground city of Nokron, to pursue her plan involving the Dark Moon.
Ranni travels to the Moonlight Altar, a remote plateau guarded by a sleeping ancient dragon coiled around a cathedral of sorcery, to claim a special ring meant for her Elden Lord consort.
Ranni leaves the Dark Moon Ring for the tarnished to retrieve and bring back to her, formally asking them to be her lord and consort.
Leda hints at a tumultuous past between the Hornsent and the tower folk, resulting from ancient conflicts instigated by Queen Marika's commands.
The Dragon Communion Priestess provides lore about Bayle and Placidusax, revealing the former dominion and decline of the Ancient Dragons.
The Fire Giants were one-eyed beings who worshipped a primitive fire god predating the Golden Order and tended a red flame of ruin capable of burning the Erdtree.
The Nox, also called the people of the eternal cities, were builders and scholars who constructed underground metropolises lit by artificial stars.
The Crucible Knights are ancient warriors who served under Godfrey but whose design and incantations point to a time before the Golden Order existed.
The Misbegotten were strong, winged beings who were later enslaved under the Golden Order.
The Omens were beings born bearing physical traits of the old Crucible, such as horns, which the Golden Order later declared signs of corruption.
Marika constructed the Golden Order, a system of divine law and metaphysics based on the runes composing the Elden Ring.
The Night's Cavalry represent an old knightly tradition that predates the Golden Order's reorganization of martial culture around the Erdtree.
The Golden Order, established by Queen Marika when brought to the Lands Between by the Greater Will, is the most dominant faction in the land.
The Night's Cavalry serve the night itself rather than any specific lord or institution, and have patrolled the same routes since before the Shattering.
The Black Knife Assassins were an elite group of Numen women with mysterious ties to Marika, armed with death-imbued knives and wearing near-invisible cloaked armor.
The Golden Order built these guardians to ensure that what happened within the roots of the Erdtree stayed hidden there.
Those Who Live in Death are the numerous undead in the Lands Between whose existence violates the Golden Order's framework of mortality, leading to their persecution and hunting by the Order.
Rykard's Volcano Manor became a refuge for assassins and recusants who rejected the Golden Order and hunted tarnished.
The Greater Will effectively went silent after the Shattering, unable or unwilling to guide events.
Mohg recruited followers for the Mohgwyn Dynasty, offering deals to some like Bloody Finger Okina and kidnapping others like the War Surgeons.
Rykard's philosophy at Volcano Manor encourages followers to consume the flesh of gods as an act of ultimate blasphemy against the Golden Order.
After the Shattering and the Greater Will's departure, some Golden Order followers began questioning the Order's infallibility.
Volcano Manor sends the player to assassinate targets who threaten Rykard's own project, showing his disregard for solidarity with other Tarnished.
The Golden Order tolerated sorcery as useful and kept it controlled through the Academy of Raya Lucaria, despite tension between sorcery's cosmic independence and Golden Order theology.
Omen bosses found in Leyndell's sewers represent a community of Omens who built their own culture after being cast out by Golden Order society.
The Two Fingers are disembodied hands of the Greater Will that communicate through a sign language understood only by trained finger readers, and they select mortal Empyrean candidates for godhood.
Followers of the Frenzied Flame are scarred, one-eyed people whose eyes burn with yellow fire, believing the end of everything would be a mercy.
Tanith is now the Lady of the Volcano Manor, recruiting Tarnished willing to rise against the Greater Will and become recusants.
Recusants who prove themselves worthy at Volcano Manor are granted an audience with Rykard, where they are devoured by him and become part of the Volcano Manor family.
Volcano Manor houses a group of Recusant Tarnished led by Praetor Rykard, seeking to rebel against the Erdtree.
Volcano Manor's notable members include Bernahl, Tanith, Patches, Praetor Rykard, and Rya.
The Mohgwyn Dynasty is led by Mohg, Lord of Blood, and like Volcano Manor its members invade other Tarnished and renounce the Greater Will, but bloodshed is their sole motive.
The beginnings of the Mohgwyn Dynasty can be found at Mohgwyn Palace, and its notable members include Mohg and White Mask Varre.
The Carian Royal Family faction's remaining members are Rennala, Ranni, and their trusted advisors after the Academy's scholars rebelled.
Serving the Carian royal family now means serving Ranni in her mission to usurp the Two Fingers and Greater Will, rebelling against her fate as an Empyrean.
Notable members of the Carian Royal Family faction include Blaidd, Preceptor Seluvis, Ranni the Witch, Rennala, and War Counsellor Iji.
Members sympathetic to Those Who Live in Death await the rise of their Lord, Godwyn, Prince of Death, the first of the dead demigods.
Fia is a notable member associated with Those Who Live in Death.
Notable Golden Order members include Brother Corhyn, D Hunter of the Dead, D's Twin Brother, Goldmask, Kenneth Haight, Radagon, and Queen Marika.
The Frenzied Flame is a covert faction led by the Three Fingers, who serve an unknown Outer God that rejects the Greater Will and blames it for the world's problems.
Frenzied Flame followers await a Lord of Chaos who will burn the world down to end its troubles.
Notable Frenzied Flame members include Hyetta, Nomadic Merchants, the Three Fingers, and Shabriri.
The Hornsent is both an individual character and the name of a race originating from the Realm of Shadow.

Marika was originally a Newman (Numen), a rare people noted for unusual constitutions, chosen as an Empyrean candidate by the Two Fingers and brought from outside the Lands Between to become a god at the Gate of Divinity in Anor Ilim, serving the Greater Will as its vassal.
Placidusax was the Elden Lord of a world that predated the current cosmological order established by the Greater Will.
Placidusax has two heads, one representing a dragon god who abandoned the world and never returned, for whom Placidusax has waited ever since.

Godfrey, originally a chieftain named Hoarah Loux from the Badlands and an extraordinarily powerful warrior consumed by a lust for battle, was the first human Marika chose as her consort because he was the best warrior in the world, needed to conquer resisting peoples; he became the first Elden Lord and led the wars that expanded the Erdtree's dominion across the Lands Between.

Godfrey also fathered twin omen sons, Morgott and Mohg, who were hidden in the sewers beneath Leyndell because their crucible-like deformities were considered shameful; Mohg was told his crucible marks were shameful signs of corruption.
The Tarnished is a being who once possessed the grace of the Erdtree, lost it, died, and endured a strange persistence that being Tarnished grants.
Upon becoming consort, Godfrey took Beast Regent Serosh upon his back to quell his bloodlust and become more fit to be a Lord.

Before her madness, Rennala was a young astrologer who, after a chance encounter with the Full Moon, learned moon magic—a school focused on lunar energies amplifying glintstone power, studied through empirical investigation rather than Golden Order faith—and became head of the Academy of Raya Lucaria and one of the most celebrated and powerful sorcerers of her age, known as Queen of the Full Moon.
Malenia was cursed with scarlet rot from birth, marked by the God of Scarlet Rot, a corruption she had no choice in that eventually consumed her eye, arm, and leg.

Miquella was cursed with eternal youth, forever trapped in a child's body, unable to grow into the mature form required for godhood; his goal, revealed in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, is to become a god of compassion and establish a new order free of the Greater Will by completing a ritual involving capturing Radahn's soul and placing it into Mohg's body.

Ranni renounced her flesh and transferred her soul into a porcelain doll modeled after a mentor she loved, dying in the flesh on the Night of the Black Knives to preserve the freedom of her soul, allowing her consciousness to survive and continue scheming.

Godwyn the Golden, firstborn son of Godfrey and Marika, was regarded as the kindest and best of the demigods, noted for his nobility and warmth, and formed a genuine bond of friendship with the dragon Fortissax, before being killed in a way that destroyed his soul while his body persisted, becoming the Prince of Death.
Miquella envisioned a world without discrimination that would welcome those rejected by the Golden Order, including albinaurics, the misbegotten, and omens.
Messmer the Impaler is Marika's son, born with an affinity for serpentine flame and cursed with the Abyssal Serpent inside him, who was erased from official history similarly to Godwyn's erasure.
Maliketh, the Black Blade, is Marika's Shadow, bestowed on her by the Greater Will as an Empyrean (similar to how Blaidd is Ranni's Shadow), described as her devoted shadow and puppy.

Morgott and his twin Mohg were born Omens, bearing horns and talons considered abominations by the Golden Order, and were cast into the sewers beneath Leyndell as children, sons of Godfrey and Marika.

Mohg is Morgott's twin brother; both were Omens cast into the sewers, but unlike Morgott, Mohg fully embraced his accursed Omen nature, choosing a different path and receiving the favor of the Formless Mother, the Outer God of Blood.

Godfrey served the Golden Order with absolute commitment and was exiled for having run out of wars to fight; afterward he reverted to being Hoarah Loux, wandering and fighting for the pure pleasure of combat while waiting for Marika's promise to be fulfilled.
Miquella developed a theology of 'unalloyed gold,' a form of divine power independent of the Greater Will, and used it to grow the Haligtree as a sanctuary.
Starscourge Radahn was regarded as the strongest demigod in raw combat capability.

Radahn learned an entire school of gravitational magic to hold the stars still and lock the constellations in place because his sister Ranni's fate was tied to the movement of a specific star, preventing an unwanted destiny.
Radahn held the stars still for centuries because he resented Ranni's choices and loved his mother Rennala.

Radahn, a massive lion-armored general, studied gravitational magic in Sellia, a town in Caelid known for sorcerers who studied stars and cosmic forces, partly so he could make himself lighter and still be carried by his small horse Leonard, whom he'd owned since childhood, rather than giving up riding him.

Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, a human sorcerer and head of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, became connected to the demigod lineage by marrying Radagon after he defeated her sorcerers in battle and proposed peace through union; they had three children together: Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni.

Radagon eventually left Rennala and their children to return to his duty as Marika's other self (since Marika and Radagon are the same being), leaving Rennala in grief and effectively abandoned, though she does not consciously realize this.

Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, son of Rennala and Radagon, deliberately fed himself to a god-devouring serpent and merged with it to become both human and serpent, presiding over Mt. Gelmir and turning Volcano Manor into a haven for rebels and assassins who reject the Greater Will's authority.

Rykard believed the Erdtree and Golden Order were a lie—that Marika ruled by force—and sought to resist and overthrow them by becoming immortal through consuming divine power rather than worshiping it.
Godrick the Grafted is the most distant, weakest descendant of Godfrey's bloodline among the demigods, considered least powerful in terms of inherited divine power.
Godrick grafts the limbs of other creatures, people, and conquered warriors onto his own body to compensate for what he believes is his inadequate, weak inherited divine power.
Godrick claims to have trained under Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, though the game never confirms whether this claim is true.
Malenia, Miquella's sworn protector and champion, has never been defeated in any battle, including her closest encounter at the Battle of Aeonia against Radahn.
Morgott's dialogue suggests he once attempted to claim the throne of Elden Lord himself but was warded off by the Erdtree.

Mohg built the Mohgwyn Dynasty, a blood-soaked realm dedicated to the Formless Mother, and kidnapped Miquella, hoping to raise him to full godhood and become his consort to claim the title of monarch, since Mohg himself is not an Empyrean.
After the Battle of Aeonia, Malenia went to guard the Haligtree, her brother Miquella's abandoned sanctuary, in his absence, having given everything for his cause and still waiting for him to return.
Vyke, a tarnished, was according to item descriptions closer to becoming Elden Lord than anyone before the player character.

Morgott conceals his Omen nature and disguises himself as Margit to hunt those who threaten the Golden Order before they reach Leyndell, first confronting the Tarnished under this pseudonym at Stormveil Castle.
Nepheli's questline involves confronting the horror of Stormveil's population being experimented on and turned into shambling creatures by Godrick.

Rennala is found in the ruined Grand Library, surrounded by loyal students, singing a lullaby while clutching an amber egg (containing a shard of the Elden Ring) given to her by Radagon as a parting gift, which she believes still contains him, refusing to accept his departure.
The students at the Academy of Raya Lucaria remain devoted to Rennala even in her grief-stricken, barely present state.
Radahn's soldiers have camped in Caelid since the Battle of Aeonia, refusing to leave or kill him out of love, waiting for a worthy opponent to end his suffering.

Despite being an Omen shunned and reviled by Leyndell his entire life and rejected by the Golden Order, Morgott eventually escaped his confinement in the sewers and dedicated himself to protecting the city and remains its most devoted champion, defending a throne he was never allowed to sit on.

Melina's personal goal, only understood at the end of the story, is to sacrifice herself as kindling to burn open the Erdtree so the Tarnished can enter it; at the Forge of the Giants she does so, stating she does not know what she will become but does not regret the choice.

Messmer remained loyal to Marika throughout his long war, never developing the perspective to question that loyalty; despite being abandoned by her, he continues his mission and becomes a dominant figure in the Realm of Shadow.

Sir Ansbach is a former servant of Mohg, once part of the Pureblood Knights (though the crest on his armor has nearly faded over time), who now follows Miquella in the Realm of Shadow; despite knowing his loyalty to Mohg is neither logical nor just, he still holds onto his oath.

Alexander travels toward the Radahn Festival out of genuine joy at the prospect of fighting alongside great warriors, and at the end of his questline requests to be defeated by the player so his absorbed essence can be carried forward.

Redmane Freyja is a former loyalist of General Radahn, having fought alongside him in past battles, who has since become a devoted follower of Miquella after he healed a scarlet rot wound on her face, leaving a permanent scar she now views as her guiding compass and new purpose.

Freyja recalls fighting alongside Radahn and expresses readiness to fight again when first meeting the Tarnished, urging them to follow Miquella's footprints, the path she herself now walks, and feels a duty to understand and honor the vow Miquella made with Radahn.

Key NPCs met in the Realm of Shadow include Needle Knight Leda, a loyal follower of Miquella; Redmane Freyja, a former Radahn warrior; a Hornsent representative; and Sir Ansbach, a former servant of Mohg; early in the DLC it is revealed these characters were united under Miquella's charm, and when he breaks a rune arc to free them, the group becomes divided and uncertain, revealing his manipulative side.
Miquella possesses a supernatural charm that compels affection from others, including demigods, which he has used deliberately to further his goals.
Sellen was expelled/exiled from the Academy of Raya Lucaria for conducting heretical, forbidden research into the primeval currents of sorcery predating the Academy's systematized magic.
Sellen's true identity and history with Raya Lucaria are revealed across her questline, showing she is connected to something older than the Academy itself.
Sorceress Sellen was one of the most promising sorcerers in the history of Raya Lucaria Academy and had a unique glintstone crown.
Master Lusat and Master Azur were other primeval sorcerers banished from the Academy, and both had their minds broken by glimpsing the primeval current.

According to Jerren, Sellen has killed many fellow sorcerers in her studies and was a longstanding enemy of the Carian family who had committed atrocities against fellow sorcerers; Jerren promised Ranni and Iji he would slay her.
Sellen was imprisoned in Witchbane Ruins by the Academy and the Carian Royal Family due to her forbidden pursuits.
The Tarnished can help Sellen transplant her primeval glintstone, essentially her soul, into another compatible body to free her.
Seluvis helped Sellen in some way when she was initially exiled from the academy, though Sellen does not seem fond of him.
Rykard was served by the Gelmir Knights, and the lava sorceries usable by the Tarnished were created by him, some derived from old Mt. Gelmir hexes.
According to the Stone of Gurranq, Maliketh was a ferocious warrior whose name meant 'Death of the Demigods'.
Maliketh's Remembrance implies he was betrayed by Marika, though the details are unknown.
It is heavily implied that the Beast Clergyman found in Crumbling Farum Azula is Gurranq himself, and that Gurranq is Maliketh, the Black Blade.
Godwyn's incomplete death produced an entity called the Death Prince, combining Godwyn's lingering flesh presence with the rune of death.
Radagon, characterized by flowing red hair which he reportedly hated the tint of, was Queen Marika's second chosen consort and a great warrior.
A statue in the Royal Capital reveals that Marika and Radagon are one and the same being.
Ranni was an Empyrean, a candidate to become the next god of the Lands Between under the Greater Will; although not born a demigod, she became eligible due to Radagon's unity with Marika.
Ranni wanted to escape the fate chosen for her by the Two Fingers and refused to continue Marika's cycle of divine control.
Miquella's connection to St. Trina, revealed in the DLC, shows they are two manifestations of the same being, echoing the duality of Radagon and Marika.
Miquella's compassion was genuine, but his methods were controlling and manipulative in ways his good intentions do not fully excuse.
Mohg believed he was a devoted caretaker enabling Miquella's ascension and expected to be made his consort.

Nepheli Loux is the granddaughter of, and adoptive daughter to, Gideon Ofnir, the all-knowing leader of the Round Table Hold faction, who took her in when she became Tarnished after losing grace; she is also the adopted daughter of Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, who named her his heir even in exile.
Nepheli Loux loses faith in Sir Gideon Ofnir after learning he orchestrated the attack on the Village of the Albinaurics.
It is speculated that Nepheli Loux has ties to Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, based on sharing the surname Loux with Hoarah Loux and Kenneth Haight deeming her worthy to lead Limgrave.

Kenneth Haight is a member of Erdtree royalty and self-proclaimed rightful leader of Limgrave, owner of Fort Haight, who looks down on Godrick for his cowardly actions during the Shattering and for lacking proper lineage to rule.
After retaking Fort Haight, Kenneth Haight seeks an eligible candidate to rule Limgrave and eventually finds Nepheli Loux.

Fia, the Deathbed Companion, resides in the Round Table Hold, is empathetic toward Those Who Live in Death and considers herself their guardian, and offers an embrace that grants a buff and a debuff simultaneously.

Fia collects deathbeds, the moments of heroes' final rest, carrying them inside her body, hoping to eventually create the Prince of Death made possible by Godwyn's incomplete demise; she was driven from her home when awoken by the guidance of grace, and is devoted to the cause of those who live wrongfully in death, holding dying Tarnished in her arms out of compassion because she believed someone needed to.
A Deathbed Companion receives warmth and life from champions and then lies with the remains of an exalted noble to revive them, a practice revered in Fia's homeland.
Fia's champions include Rogier and Lionel the Lionhearted, a knight who claims to be her father.

By combining Ranni's half of the Cursemark of Death from the Divine Tower of Liurnia with Godwyn's half from D, Fia implies Godwyn could be reborn as the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince through her role as his Deathbed Companion.

Melina walks beside the Tarnished as a guide, tending the Sites of Grace that serve as checkpoints across the world, offering fragments of information and a kindness that seems genuine despite being largely unexplained; she has no grace of her own and no permanent vessel, appearing only through temporary forms she chooses, as though existing at the margins of the world rather than at its center.

Melina describes herself as someone born at the foot of the Erdtree who was given a purpose by her mother, implied to be Marika; she can recall echoes of Queen Marika's past actions and words when spoken to at Sites of Grace.
Melina may be a child of Marika existing outside conventional demigod lineages, or a soul given form by the Erdtree, or a deliberate contingency created by Marika.

Melina holds contempt for the Frenzied Flame and believes its lord is no true Lord; if the Tarnished takes the Frenzied Flame before the event at the Forge of the Giants, she will leave and threaten to deliver Destined Death.
Goldmask's revelation, reached using the Mending Rune of Perfect Order, is that the flaws of the Golden Order come from the fact that gods are as flawed and fickle as the mortals they govern.

Goldmask sat in silence at the edge of a great ruin, working out the nature of the universe without writing anything down, believing the right person would understand without words; he is a famed scholar of Golden Order fundamentalism who does not speak, communicating instead through rhythmic hand and finger movements.
Goldmask once lamented that hunters of Those Who Live in Death had become fanatics who hunted merely to have an evil to fight.

The Dung Eater has committed atrocities against both the dead and the living, defiling his victims' corpses with Seedbed Curses to curse their souls from returning to the Erdtree, and wants to spread his personal curse to all beings and future generations in the Lands Between by gestating the Mending Rune of the Fell Curse, so everyone is equally defiled; he is a Tarnished who bears the heart of an Omen, as suggested by his armor.
General Radahn is described as 'the conqueror of the stars' and Malenia the Severed as 'the Blade of Miquella'.
Melina does not have a physical form and serves as the Tarnished's Finger Maiden in exchange for being taken to the Erdtree and later the Mountaintops of the Giants.

The White Masks at Mohgwyn Palace were abducted by Mohg, Lord of Blood, and turned into Bloody Fingers through a ritual involving his Omen blood; of the four White Masks encountered, only Varre was able to withstand and tame the accursed blood.

White Mask Varre remains loyal to the Mohgwyn Dynasty and tries to indoctrinate the Tarnished into it; at the end of his questline, forsaken by Mohg, he still calls out to him and blesses the Mohgwyn Dynasty as he dies.

Bloody Finger Hunter Yura is a samurai from the Land of Reeds who hunts down Bloody Fingers, some of whom have been swayed by Mohg, the Lord of Blood; his biggest target is Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger, a Tarnished he holds in high regard.
Yura warns that those who partake in Dragon Communion eventually lose their humanity.
Sorcerer Rogier was once a scholar seeking the truth behind the Night of the Black Knives; his pursuits led him under Stormveil Castle, where he disturbed a corpse and became afflicted with Death.

Unlike D, who sees Those Who Live in Death as a threat to the Golden Order, Rogier is empathetic toward them; finishing his quest reveals insights about the Night of the Black Knives before he succumbs to his affliction.

D, Hunter of the Dead is a devout follower of the Golden Order who hunts Those Who Live in Death, especially Tibia Mariners for their Deathroot, believing they violate the principles of the Golden Order and must be exterminated.

D has a twin brother, implied to be named Darian or Devin, with whom he shares the same soul and body; they have separate bodies and minds but cannot be conscious at the same time, and both found comfort in the Golden Order, the one order that did not consider them cursed.

D, Beholder of Death can be found slumbering in Siofra Aqueduct while D is alive, and grieving there if D is dead; he swears revenge on his brother's killer, whether it be Fia or the Tarnished, when given his brother's armor.
Gurranq, Beast Clergyman is a large beastman who hungers for Deathroot; D was previously in charge of hunting and providing Deathroot to Gurranq before the Tarnished took over.

Roderika is a Tarnished driven away from her home across the sea, and her cloak implies she was once royalty; she met White Mask Varre, who gave her the same advice he gives the Tarnished: to seek Godrick and his Great Rune at Stormveil Castle.
The men escorting Roderika at Stormhill were taken and sacrificed for grafting, leaving her guilt-ridden for being too afraid to join them.
Roderika moves to the Roundtable Hold and is trained by Smithing Master Hewg to become a skillful spirit tuner, staying behind with him even as the Roundtable Hold burns, to repay his kindness.

Smithing Master Hewg is a misbegotten chained and imprisoned at the Roundtable Hold, tasked by Queen Marika with forging a weapon strong enough to kill a god; he believes the Tarnished will become Elden Lord, stating so before losing his memory completely.

Gatekeeper Gostoc is the gatekeeper of Stormveil Castle who nonetheless informs the Tarnished of a safer side passage, while secretly following and stealing a portion of the Tarnished's Golden Runes each time they are defeated in the castle.
Gostoc holds contempt for Godrick, having been mistreated by him, and longs for freedom from his duties; when Nepheli Loux takes the throne, Gostoc is happy to return to his duties.
Boc the Seamster is a demi-human outcast who admires his late mother, a skilled seamstress; he was expelled from the Coastal Cave and had his possessions stolen by other demi-humans.

After the Tarnished helps Boc reclaim his Sewing Needle and Tailoring Tools, he offers to tailor their armor; the Tarnished can help him further by giving him a Larval Tear to change his appearance or by telling him he is beautiful, and he is grateful either way.

Brother Corhyn is a cleric of the Golden Order whose armor implies he once foretold an inauspicious prophecy; he leaves the Roundtable Hold in search of Goldmask, a scholar of Golden Order fundamentalism, acting as his scribe by translating his finger movements into written records.
Corhyn begins to question Goldmask's intentions after learning of his reservations toward the Golden Order.

Gowry is a Kindred of Rot disguised as an old sage and was Millicent's caretaker as a child; he found Millicent and presumably her sisters as babies in the swamp of Aeonia and raised them hoping they would become scarlet valkyries under Malenia, seeing the most potential in Millicent.
At the end of Millicent's quest, Gowry asks the Tarnished to help Millicent's sisters attack her, believing betrayal will trigger her to 'bloom'.

Millicent is a daughter of Malenia, sharing her mother's red hair, missing arm from scarlet rot, and swordsmanship style; due to scarlet rot, she does not remember her childhood with Gowry despite feeling familiarity at his shack.
After being cured with the Unalloyed Golden Needle, Millicent seeks out Malenia to help her resist the scarlet rot, but is ambushed by her sisters at Elphael before reaching her.
If defended by the Tarnished, Millicent reveals she knows what Gowry hoped she would become, then removes the golden needle and succumbs to scarlet rot to remain herself.
Irina is the blind daughter of Edgar, Commander of Castle Morne, who escaped the castle with her father's and attendants' help after the Misbegotten serving it rebelled.

Irina asks the Tarnished to deliver a letter persuading her father to leave the castle, but she is murdered before their reunion; the large sword found by her corpse implies an escaped Misbegotten from Castle Morne was her killer.

Edgar, Commander of Castle Morne, was ordained by Godrick and stays to protect the castle's Grafted Blade Greatsword even as attendants flee the Misbegotten rebellion; after finding Irina's body, he regrets failing to protect her and swears vengeance on her killers.
Edgar can later be found as an invader at Revengers Shack, and the Shabriri Grape he drops suggests he succumbed to madness from Irina's death.

Hyetta is a blind young woman who resembles Irina and can perceive light by consuming Shabriri Grapes; initially disgusted that they are human eyes, she accepts it as necessary to become a finger maiden, and mentions other beings with trembling hands and emaciated fingers have also given her the grapes.
Completing Hyetta's quest and helping her become a Finger Maiden reveals more information on the Three Fingers and the Frenzied Flame.

Shabriri is a mysterious figure calling himself chaos incarnate, inhabiting the body of Yura, who he claims willingly gave it up; when met at the Mountaintops of the Giants, he tries to persuade the Tarnished to become Lord of Frenzied Flame and shares information on the Frenzied Flame Proscription.
Ranni discovered her own full moon, Ranni's Dark Moon, and learned cold sorceries from the mysterious Snow Witch she encountered in the woods; she has held Blaidd and Iji dear since childhood.
Ranni defeated the Glintstone Dragon Adula, who then swore allegiance to her.

Ranni is introduced to the player in a tower in northern Liurnia, one of three towers belonging to her and her brothers, once her family's home before her father Radagon left to return to Marika; she appears as a young woman with pale blue skin and silver hair inhabiting a small doll body.
Ranni's retinue includes Blaidd, a half-man half-wolf sworn to serve her; Iji, an ancient blacksmith; and Sellen, a snow witch whose loyalty is complex.

Blaidd is the half-wolven Shadow of Ranni, granted to her by the Two Fingers when she became an Empyrean; his loyalty lies only with Ranni, whom he considers family, despite being an agent of the Two Fingers, and even in madness he continued to defy his fate and remain faithful to her.

War Counselor Iji is the only friendly Troll the Tarnished encounters, serving as the Carian royal family's blacksmith and as Ranni's war counselor, providing guidance on the lost city of Nokron; he has watched over Blaidd and Ranni since they were children.
Iji's Mirrorhelm implies he feared the consequences of his treachery against the Greater Will.

Preceptor Seluvis is a magic preceptor serving the Carian Royal family and currently aids Ranni in her search for the dark path, while secretly scheming to betray Ranni and add her, a demigod, to his puppet collection.
It is speculated that Seluvis and Pidia have a connection due to their shared affinity for puppets.

Merchant Kale is one of the nomadic merchants the Tarnished can buy from, acquainted with Blaidd who calls him a busybody; he describes the nomadic clan as spiteful, suggesting their summoning of the frenzied flame was an act of spite.

Witch-Hunter Jerren was originally a nomadic wanderer who became a guest of the Carian royal family, befriending Ranni, Iji, and Radahn; he wields the Flamberge, a symbol of Redmane Castle, and heralds the beginning of the war festival when first met.

Thops is a glintstone sorcerer from Raya Lucaria Academy nicknamed 'Thops the Bluntstone' for lacking talent for powerful sorceries; if aided, he completes his lifelong project, creating Thops's Barrier, a defensive glintstone sorcery that deflects sorceries and incantations back at the caster.

Miriel, Pastor of Vows is a large turtle and steward of the Church of Vows who teaches Absolution though he does not require it himself; well-versed in the history of Rennala and Radagon's union, he teaches the Tarnished sorceries and incantations and, unlike Corhyn, is open-minded toward all sorcery and incantation scrolls given to him.

Albus is a first-generation Albinauric, created with defective legs that prevented walking, and when their legs fade, their life fades too; the Tarnished finds him disguised as a pot to escape Gideon's subordinates attacking the Village of the Albinaurics.

Latenna is a first-generation Albinauric and wolf-riding archer, one of many such archers, who was interrogated by an agent of Sir Gideon Ofnir (or possibly Gideon himself) about the second half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, leading to the death of her wolf Lobo.

If approached with the right half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, Latenna asks to be taken to Apostate Derelict in exchange for the location of the left half; there she transfers a birthing droplet to a large Albinauric named Phillia, related to creating life for the Albinaurics.

Ensha of the Royal Remains is Sir Gideon Ofnir's silent right-hand man; his armor set, the Royal Remains Set, and weapon, the Clinging Bone, suggest he is the reanimated remains of a king known as the Soulless King.
It is speculated from Gideon's dialogue that Ensha was tasked with finding both halves of the Haligtree Secret Medallion and attacks the Tarnished at Roundtable Hold to take whichever half they hold.
Tanith is consort to Lord Rykard and adoptive mother of Rya; she worked as a dancer in a foreign land until she caught Lord Rykard's eye and became his consort.

Tanith stayed by Rykard's side even after he swore himself to blasphemy and merged with the God-Devouring Serpent, even when his men turned against him and even when she was offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness as an escape.

Bernahl is an Ash of War teacher the Tarnished can first meet in Stormhill, said to be a Tarnished worthy of becoming Elden Lord, following his destined path without doubt, until his maiden threw herself into 'the fire'.
The Tarnished can later find Bernahl as a recusant at Volcano Manor; after Rykard is defeated, Bernahl denounces the Greater Will and vows to fell them on behalf of his brother.
Rya's real name is Zorayas, and she is a Man-Serpent disguised as a human working as the scout for Volcano Manor; only the Tarnished and her adoptive mother Tanith know of her true serpent form.
Tanith told Rya that she was born by the grace of a great king, but Rya later becomes suspicious of Volcano Manor's secrets and confronts Tanith.
A talisman left behind at the end of Rya's questline suggests her true mother was Daedicar, a woman said to have birthed multiple grotesque children through countless acts of adultery.

Patches the Untethered is a bandit who tricks unsuspecting people into death traps and entrapment schemes; if spared, he sells the Tarnished various goods presumably looted from the corpses of those he successfully tricked, and mentions his band of bandits is made up of foot soldiers and survivors of defeated armies left to fend for themselves.
Patches has taken a liking to Tanith and risks himself to obtain the Dancer's Castanets, hoping to restore her mind after Rykard's defeat.

Diallos is the youngest son of House Hoslow and lives in the shadow of his elder brother, Juno Hoslow; unlike Juno, a formidable fighter, Diallos is timid, which does not fit his family's bloodshed-focused motto.

Despite their differences, Diallos and Juno care deeply for each other, with Juno doting on Diallos and Diallos looking up to him; Diallos hopes to become a champion like his brother but grows disillusioned and seeks a different purpose.
Jar-Bairn is a young jar living in Jarburg, a secret village of peaceful Living Jars, and one of the few Living Jars capable of speaking to the Tarnished, a warrior jar like his uncle Alexander.
Jar-Bairn can be found talking in his sleep about reuniting with Alexander, poachers destroying the Living Pots at Jarburg, or Diallos taking care of him.

Iron Fist Alexander is an older Living Jar who left Jarburg to seek great battle and hone his skills; warrior jars like him are Living Jars filled with the remains of warriors, destined to leave home and journey alone to become great champions.

Alexander the Iron Fist is a giant jar, a living vessel called a 'jarhead' containing the remains of great warriors absorbed into it; found stuck in the ground up to his shoulders, calling cheerfully for help, he wants to grow stronger by absorbing the remains of great warriors.

Blackguard Big Boggart is a Tarnished and former criminal selling boiled prawns and crabs, first at the Boilprawn Shack and later outside the royal capital; he may have previously been convicted of thievery, having stolen Rya's necklace.
Boggart used to be cellmates with Dung Eater, witnessing him defile a friend's body with the Seedbed Curse, the most harrowing experience of Boggart's life.

Enia is a Finger Reader Crone the Tarnished encounters at the Roundtable Hold, interpreting the wisdom of the Greater Will through the Two Fingers; unlike other finger readers who become frantic after losing their Two Fingers, Enia remains calm.

Despite being an agent of the Greater Will, Enia supports the Tarnished burning down the Erdtree once her Two Fingers stop communicating with her, and claims that before the Tarnished, another person had gathered two Great Runes.
Royal Knight Loretta trained in a Carian royal combat school combining physical skill and magic, and devoted herself to serving Miquella's project.
St. Trina, an enigmatic figure barely mentioned in the base game, is explored further through interactions with her and her follower Thiollier, revealing her connection to Miquella.
Freyja reflects on the complexity of potentially fighting alongside or against former allies like Sir Ansbach.

Hornsent holds a deep grudge against the Erdtree, viewing it as an enemy of his people, and views Marika as a betrayer of his people; despite his hatred, he follows an oath to Miquella and offers assistance to the player, refusing alms or gifts out of pride but rewarding the player with maps marking crosses tied to his people's suffering.
After Messmer's death, Hornsent expresses satisfaction but states his thirst for vengeance extends to Marika and the entire Erdtree.

Igon is a broken drake warrior consumed by pain and a burning need for revenge against the dread dragon Bayle, having once sought honor through Dragon Communion; his soul clings to the mountain where his battle with Bayle took place, asking the player to climb the peak and continue his fight.

When the player defeats the Jagged Peak Drake, Igon reflects on the warrior he once was before asking the player to continue his fight against Bayle; after Bayle is defeated, Igon's spirit is freed and finally able to rest, his revenge realized.
The Dragon Communion Priestess compares Igon's ambition and hunger to Bayle's fiery spirit and relentless drive, and is herself a surviving Ancient Dragon and worshipper of Dragonlord Placidusax.

Moore is a gentle giant, a follower of Miquella, and a member of the Forager Brood, a group dedicated to finding crafting materials and recipes across the Land of Shadow; when the Great Rune breaks, he is visibly affected but continues clinging to his devotion to Miquella.
Moore provides Thiollier with Black Syrup after being asked to find it, and reacts with grief and anger if a member of the forager brood is killed or harmed, calling it an unforgivable tragedy.
After the final boss is defeated, Moore laments the loss of his brood and the absence of allies including Lady Leda, Father Dane, Sir Ansbach, Freyja, Thiollier, and the Hornsent.

Needle Knight Leda is the leader of Miquella's band of followers in the Realm of Shadow; she references Dane, a silent monk who has served Miquella longer than she has, describing him as reserved but a formidable warrior.

After the Great Rune breaks, Leda grows suspicious of her fellow followers and proposes eliminating the Hornsent, fearing his vengeance could threaten Miquella's cause, and identifies Sir Ansbach, a former commander of the Pureblood Knights, as a potential danger due to his past involvement with Miquella's blood blade.
After defeating Sir Ansbach, Leda reflects on the weight of her actions but accepts them as the price for ensuring Miquella's continued favor.

Thiollier is a non-combatant Tarnished character skilled in crafting poison rather than fighting, found at the Pillar Path Cross Site of Grace, who serves Miquella and mentions Lady Leda when first met, acknowledging shared devotion to the same deity.

After the Great Rune breaks, Thiollier becomes haunted by memories of St. Trina, the goddess of slumber, and longs for her poison to grant him eternal sleep, traveling south to find her resting place and becoming increasingly obsessive and erratic, eventually turning hostile if the player tries to speak for her.

Hornsent Grandam belongs to the ancient Hornsent race that once thrived in Belurat Tower Settlement and was connected to the Divine Beast Dancing Lion; he greets the Tarnished with suspicion, accusing them of complicity in Messmer's atrocities.
Dryleaf Dane is a master of unarmed martial combat, a devoted follower of Miquella, and a sworn ally of Leda.

Count Ymir is the High Priest of Manus Metyr Cathedral and a vendor for glintstone sorceries, sharing philosophical musings about the Greater Will, the Erdtree, and the world's flaws; his companion Jolán can be summoned during specific encounters once her questline advances.

Jolán is a loyal warrior serving Count Ymir, found standing on a pillar beside him in the Cathedral of Manus Metyr; she warns the player that crossing Ymir will bring regret, calls him a guiding star in the dark sky, and will fight to protect his will if he is betrayed or harmed.
Fire Knight Queelign is a knight loyal to Queen Marika, introduced in the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, first encountered as an NPC invader in Belurat Tower Settlement and the Church of Crusade.
The Fire Giants lived at the Mountaintops of the Giants, a frozen region at the world's highest point.
The Land of Shadow is a dark realm obscured by the Erdtree where the goddess Marika first set foot.
The throne room of Stormveil Castle is decorated with writhing masses of flesh and limbs from people incorporated into the castle walls, symbolizing Godrick's philosophy of accumulating strength.
Stormveil Castle appears grand and powerful but shows signs of crumbling maintenance and disorganized defenses, reflecting Godrick's desperation.
Mohg's arena, Moghwyn Palace, is covered in scarlet blood representing the Formless Mother's physical presence spread across his domain.
Leyndell is built around the Erdtree's massive golden roots, which arch through the city like exposed bones.
Leyndell has been sealed off from normal time, its remaining soldiers and knights still loyal to an order that no longer functions since the Shattering.
The Lake of Rot will kill a person almost instantly if they remain immersed in it for more than a few moments.
Patches' Emporium can be accessed upon reaching Volcano Manor.

The Realm of Shadow is divided into ten distinct areas: Gravesite Plain, Scadu Altus, Rauh Base, Ancient Ruins of Rauh, Cerulean Coast, Charo's Hidden Grave, Jagged Peak, Abyssal Woods, Finger Ruins of Rhia, and Scaduview.
The Hornsent character is found with Freyja at the Three-Path Cross in Gravesite Plain.
Moore can first be encountered at the Main Gate Cross Site of Grace near Belurat Tower Settlement, accompanied by Sir Ansbach.
Leda is found at the Highroad Cross Site of Grace near Hornsent.
St. Trina is located in the deepest part of Stone Coffin Fissure, within the Garden of Deep Purple.
The Elden Beast's essence became the Elden Ring, a cosmic entity that was never forged but existed as a living expression of cosmic law.
Hoarah Loux took on the golden lion spirit Serosh, the Beast Regent, which lived on his shoulders and suppressed his violent nature, allowing him to become Godfrey, the first Elden Lord.
As tradition dictates, Rennala bestowed a Moon Greatsword upon her spouse Radagon, who after returning to Marika reforged it into the Golden Order Greatsword.
Miquella gave Malenia a needle made of unalloyed gold that suppressed her Scarlet Rot, though he could not cure it.

Marika entrusted Maliketh with guarding the Rune of Death, the principle of true permanent mortality, after removing it from the Elden Ring following Godwyn's death, sealing it inside her shadowbound beast.
Rennala's Great Rune is called the Great Rune of the Unborn and allows the recipient to be reborn as something different, which functions in-game as the ability to respec character stats.
Sellen's questline involves gathering primal glintstone, crystallized consciousness of ancient powerful sorcerers.
The Finger-Slayer Blade was forged specifically to kill the Fingers, the cosmic emissaries of the Greater Will.
When summoned, Melina wields the Blade of Calling, a dagger previously owned by a kindling maiden.
Blaidd's sword, the Royal Greatsword, was imbued with cold magic as proof of his loyalty to Ranni.
According to Jerren, the blades smithed by Iji were blunt but resistant to decay from scarlet rot.
The Graven-School Talisman notes that fashioning sorcerers' bodies into 'seeds of stars' is one method of pursuing the primeval current, suggesting the practice requires human sacrifice.
Albus safeguards the right half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, said to be key to reaching Miquella's Haligtree, the Albinaurics' promised land.
Living Jar Shards contain traces of magical power and fetch high prices, making Living Jars a target for poachers.
The Ironjar Aromatic is a forbidden defense-boosting consumable made from Living Jar Shards by Depraved Perfumers.
The Glintstone Kris symbolizes the unity between the Capital of Leyndell and the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
Mohg used his weapon, Mohgwyn's Sacred Spear, to further communicate with the Formless Mother.
The Blasphemous Claw, a gift from his sister Ranni, allows Rykard to challenge Maliketh as a last resort.
Throughout the Land of Shadow, players find crosses symbolizing pieces of Miquella's being that he sheds in preparation for rebirth.
Ansbach's attire slightly boosts abilities related to blood magic and dynastic skills.
Freyja's armor bears a black woolen mantle and golden markings symbolizing her past rank in Radahn's forces.
Freyja carries the Golden Lion Shield, a symbol awarded to only the most valorous knights of Radahn's personal guard.
Igon's armor set, Igon's Set, is mismatched and tattered, reflecting his past as a battlefield scavenger.
Igon's Furled Finger is a gnarled, discolored finger item that can be used to summon Igon to battle.
Thiollier warns the player not to follow his example, as St. Trina's poison would plunge them into eternal slumber.
Dryleaf Dane leaves a Monk's Missive inviting challengers to test their worth against him in the eastern lands.
Count Ymir gifts the player the Hole-Laden Necklace and a Ruins Map early in his questline.
Queelign's spirit can be summoned using the Fire Knight Queelign item, an ashen remains, causing him to attack immediately with his fiery greatsword.
St. Trina was referenced in the base game through item descriptions such as St. Trina's Torch, hinting at her connection to Miquella.
The Black Knife Assassins fight using blades carrying the influence of the Rune of Death.
In battle, Ansbach uses the Furious Blade of Ansbach, an incantation summoning a bloodflame blade that he lunges with to strike enemies, becoming stronger when charged.
Ansbach also wields the Obsidian Lamina, a slender scythe relying on skill rather than tricks.

Freyja wields a Greatsword decorated with a mane, reflecting her connection to Radahn and her strength as a warrior, and carries the Golden Lion Shield, a symbol of Radahn's personal guard awarded to only his most valorous knights.
Igon created his own weapon, Igon's Harpoon, a great arrow adorned with sharp gravel stone pieces designed to be deadly against dragons.
Igon's Greatbow is crafted from dragon bones bound with rope and scarred by claws, enhancing the power of his harpoons.
Queelign's Greatsword was remade by Queelign in the shape of the lance once wielded by his liege, symbolizing his desire to become a second Impaler.

Dragonlord Placidusax is the oldest boss in the game, a multi-headed ancient dragon who once served as an Elden Lord of a previous age under a god that vanished when the Greater Will arrived; he is found in a pocket of stopped time within crumbling Farum Azula, a realm of ruins floating in an eternal storm outside the flow of time, waiting eternally for a god that will never return.
The Ancestor Spirits are spiritual representatives of the Crucible Age, a time before the Erdtree when species boundaries were fluid.
Messmer, Mother of Fingers is revealed to be the original source of all Two Fingers and Three Fingers found throughout the Lands Between.
Lansseax was worshipped by the Gelmir Cavalry, a warrior culture that maintained the old Draconic faith against the Golden Order.
The Regal Ancestor Spirit is found in Nokron, the underground Eternal City of the Nox people, who were cast below ground by the Greater Will for trying to create their own Elden Ring.
The Fire Giant is the last survivor of the giants, a people who worshipped the Fell God and were destroyed in a war waged by Marika due to their flame challenging the Erdtree's dominance.
The Fire Giant had his legs severed and was chained to the Forge of the Giants, forced to maintain the flame of his destroyed people's faith.
Because the death curse mark was split, Godwyn's soul died but his body remained alive, corrupting and spreading underground as a growth known as the Prince of Death.

Margit, the Fell Omen, is Morgott, the Omen King, in disguise; Morgott took his lineage's Great Rune to Leyndell and placed himself on the Elden Throne as a guardian rather than Elden Lord, disguising himself as the merchant and prophet Margit to warn tarnished away from the capital and test their worthiness before revealing his true identity as guardian of the throne.
Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, took his Great Rune to Volcano Manor and merged with a great serpent, becoming a god-devouring blasphemy.
Radahn, the Starscourge, claimed his Great Rune and continued holding the stars in place using gravity magic.
Radahn survived the battle but the scarlet rot consumed his mind, reducing him to a feral, mindless creature that ate corpses.

Fortissax was the dragon companion of Godwyn the Golden; after Godwyn was murdered on the Night of the Black Knives, Fortissax descended into the Erdtree's roots to fight the spreading Deathblight and protect Godwyn's remains, remaining loyal to him even through his transformation into the Prince of Death — an unwinnable battle it still fights eternally, never having won.

Godrick the Grafted retreated to Stormveil Castle after inheriting his Great Rune and began grafting the limbs of conquered enemies onto his own body; in the second phase of his boss fight, he grafts a dragon's head onto a severed arm to gain additional power.

Mohg, Lord of Blood, built Mohgwyn Palace around a wound in the world tied to the Formless Mother, using her gifts to build a blood dynasty and declaring himself Lord of Blood; he kidnapped Miquella to use him as a vehicle for his own ascension.
The boss fight against Rennala takes place in a dream-like golden night sky space formed from her memories and power.
Fortissax attacks with golden lightning associated with Godwyn, reflecting his grief and vigil over his lost companion.
Messmer, Mother of Fingers is found broken in the Land of Shadow, her connection to the Greater Will severed or compromised.
When Godfrey returns during the Shattering, he first appears as a ghost challenging the player in Leyndell, then later as his full human self after the Erdtree's thorns fall.

Godfrey's second phase reveals Hoarah Loux, the berserker name and identity he held before Marika elevated him into the Elden Lord; near the end of the fight he tears the spirit Serosh from his shoulders, killing his restrainer and becoming his unrestrained primal self again.
The Hoarah Loux phase fights bare-armed with grappling and throwing techniques, reflecting a combat style from before civilization formalized it.
Malenia's second phase causes scarlet rot to bloom into flower-like growths around her as she stops containing the god within her.
In the Fire Giant's second phase, he tears off his own leg to expose the flame within his body.
Radagon, fought as the second-to-last boss of the main game, is revealed to be the same divine being as Marika, sharing one divine body.
Radagon fights using holy power drawn from the Golden Order's fundamental energies.
The red-gold nails embedded in Radagon's body are self-inflicted, representing his attempt to fuse himself with the Elden Ring through divine will, which ultimately failed.
When fought in the ruined desert north of Redmane Castle, Radahn still rides Leonard even while feral and consumed by rot.
Leonard stays beside Radahn's body after his death.
Malenia wakes only when the tarnished disturbs her after navigating the Consecrated Snowfield and the corrupted Haligtree.
Upon waking, Malenia says: "I dreamt for so long. My flesh was dull gold and my blood was rot," and "I await him still," referring to Miquella.
Malenia introduces herself as Malenia, Blade of Miquella, and declares she has never known defeat.
Inside the Erdtree, the Tarnished confronts Radagon, described as Marika's other, devoted half who tried to repair what Marika broke.

After Radagon falls in battle, he transforms into Marika and then into the Elden Beast, which emerges from his body; the Elden Beast was sent to the Lands Between by the Greater Will to carry the Elden Ring and is the living embodiment of its Order.
The Elden Beast is fought as a creature of golden starlight within a void of absolute darkness.
The Elden Beast is described as the living physical form of the Golden Order itself, functioning as a law rather than a conscious monster.
Astel, Naturalborn of the Void, is an alien being that arrived in the Lands Between inside a meteor and did not originate from the world's own cosmology.
Two versions of Astel appear in the game: one in the Lake of Rot and one at the end of Ranni's questline.
Astel's body resembles a star-formed crustacean with a vast insectoid face, operating on alien logic unrelated to the Golden Order or Crucible.

The Frenzied Flame Proscriber, also called the Three Fingers Servant, is represented in-game by frenzied flame enemies and the Three Fingers in Leyndell's undercity rather than as a single named boss.
Crucible Knight Siluria is found in the Deeproot Depths and is among the most ancient Crucible Knights, guarding a space tied to the oldest history of the Lands Between.

Ulcerated Tree Spirits are the transformed bodies of beings who offered themselves to the Erdtree's grace but were rejected, yet still had grace energy flow through them, creating animated corruption.
The glintstone dragons Smarag and Adula are ancient dragons whose bodies have become partially crystalline through long exposure to glintstone, letting them channel starlight through their breath.
Royal Knight Loretta is found guarding the entrance to the Haligtree in the Consecrated Snowfield, and also appears as a summonable spirit ash.
The Tibia Mariner is a skeletal boatman found across the Lands Between who commands undead armies and summons an ancient dragon turtle in some fights.
The Tibia Mariner represents a boatman tasked with ferrying souls to the afterlife, still attempting this duty in a world where Marika's removal of the Rune of Death made death inconsistent.
The Grafted Scion, fought at the start of the game, is a creature made entirely of assembled arms and weapons with no original body remaining, reflecting Godrick's grafting philosophy.
The Fell Twins are enormous Omen bosses found in optional underground areas, representing Omens who grew unmanaged and unprotected unlike demigod Omens such as Morgott and Mohg.
Romina, Saint of the Bud, is a being of scarlet rot connected to the Land of Shadow's history and the rot's ongoing presence in the world.
Bayle the Dread is the most powerful ancient dragon encountered outside Farum Azula, pursued by veteran dragon slayer Eygon for vengeance.
Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame, was a nobleman who came to the Land of Shadow seeking something and instead encountered the Three Fingers, leading to his dissolution into the Frenzied Flame.

The Scadutree Avatar is the Great Guardian of the Scadutree, a shadow tree counterpart to the Erdtree that grows in the Land of Shadow in a realm alongside, not within, the Golden Order's world, connected to Marika's hidden origins.

Commander Gaius is a boar-riding general in the Land of Shadow fully devoted to military service under Messmer's campaign, riding an enormous armored boar through the Scadutree region and fighting with tactical precision, identifying the player simply as a problem within his patrol duties.
The Red Wolf of Radagon guards the Debate Parlor in the Academy of Raya Lucaria and fights using Radagon's own sorcerous techniques.
Godskin Noble and Godskin Apostle belong to a religious order dedicated to slaying gods and wearing their skin, with its founding and theology left unexplained by the game.
In Rennala's boss fight, the first phase requires breaking the students carrying her protective golden light, while the second phase has her summon creatures reborn through her Great Rune of rebirth.
Rennala's second-phase summons include a reborn Glintstone Dragon and a troll, among other legendary creatures given new forms through her rebirth power.
Erdtree Avatars found at minor Erdtrees grow directly out of the trees themselves, acting as the Erdtree's own ambulatory immune response.
