Valiant Gargoyles are stone constructs animated by Golden Order power that guard the coffin leading to the Deeproot Depths and Godwyn's resting place.
The Mimic Tear is a silver tear of living mercury native to the eternal cities of the Nox, encountered in Nokron, that copies the player's exact appearance, weapons, and spells.
Rykard's serpent god boss form represents the complete expression of what Rykard became after fully merging with the serpent he devoured, rather than wearing a human face.
A human voice speaks through Rykard's serpent form, indicating that a vestige of Rykard's own consciousness persists and still chooses to act even from within the god-devouring serpent's body.
The Night's Cavalry Leader is the most powerful of the Night's Cavalry, a group encountered only after dark at specific locations.
Demi-Human Queen Gilika and her variants lead groups of Demi-Human enemies and represent one of many peoples of the Lands Between who exist outside the Golden Order's framework of value.
Malenia, the Blighted Bloom and her variants are beings of scarlet rot that have taken a plant-like, flower form, combining biological lushness with cosmic corruption.

Divine Beast Dancing Lion is a sacred construct rather than a natural animal, built to embody wild divine power using storm, snow, and thunder, reflecting the Land of Shadow's more reciprocal relationship with nature compared to the Golden Order.
Relena, Twin Moon Knight is found in Castle Ensis and wields both golden and cold moon magic, representing a tradition of moon sorcery that parallels Rennala's in a different context.
Putrescent Knight guards the Cerulean Coast, defending a space of beauty that is already affected by rot and dissolution.
The Putrescent Knight's armor is encrusted with evidence of decay, showing it is partly consumed by the same dissolution process it was appointed to guard against, yet it continues its duty.
Romina, Saint of the Bud embodies rot as a form of growth and renewal rather than simple decay, with her arena filling with rot blooms as the fight progresses.
The Crucible Knights fighting in Crumbling Farum Azula are ancient Crucible entities that predate the Lands Between's current structure and even the Erdtree itself.

The Stone Digger Troll, found in the Old Altus Tunnel, and other troll enemies belong to a tradition of giant humanoid beings that predates the Golden Order's specific social organization, and function primarily as laborers valued for their size and strength in mining operations, construction, and heavy infrastructure work.
Godrick's soldiers include pumpkin-headed warriors whose exaggerated design reflects an aesthetic of performed, rather than genuine, strength.

The Crucible Knights predate the Erdtree's dominance and carry Crucible aspects, such as tails and wings, that the Golden Order has long tried to suppress; different variants, such as the Tail Knight and Wing Knight, express different ancient biological lineages made possible during the Crucible Age.
Death Birds are enormous feathered creatures that only appear after dark, belonging to an order of death and time that predates the Golden Order's management of death.
The Night's Cavalry are armored riders appearing only at night, tied to a knightly tradition predating the Golden Order.

Bell Bearing Hunters appear at night at the locations of wandering merchants, attacking anyone present and carrying bell bearings that let the player later buy the merchant's wares from an NPC after the hunters are defeated.
After Melina's sacrifice, the base game does not fully resolve what happens to her, leaving it ambiguous whether she is gone or transformed.
If the Tarnished has accepted the Frenzied Flame, Melina does not sacrifice herself and instead becomes a figure sworn to deliver the Tarnished's destined death.
After the Elden Beast falls, the Elden Ring lies shattered and Marika appears fractured and silent, awaiting the Tarnished's choice of ending.
Nepheli's questline resolves with her ruling a restored Limgrave from its throne, presented as one of the game's unambiguously positive outcomes.
The Age of Fracture ending has the Tarnished mend the Elden Ring without additional power or intention, becoming Elden Lord while the Golden Order and Greater Will's structure continue as before.
The Age of Order ending requires completing the questlines of Brother Corhyn and Goldmask.
Goldmask's mending rune creates a transcendental Golden Order meant to rise above the corruption of individual divine personalities.
The Age of Duskyn ending comes from completing the questline of Fia, the Deathbed Companion, who holds Tarnished in her embrace to share in their life force.
Fia's mending rune restores natural death to the world, allowing those who live in death to finally rest and ending the Erdtree's cycle of capturing and recycling souls.
The Blessing of Despair ending comes from the Dung Eater's questline.
The Blessing of Despair ending is considered the darkest of the Elden Lord endings, reflecting a nihilistic worldview given power over reality.
The Lord of the Frenzied Flame ending requires descending beneath Leyndell's sewers to find the Three Fingers and allow them to grant the Frenzied Flame.
Accepting the Frenzied Flame locks the Tarnished into becoming the Lord of Chaos, the instrument of the Frenzied Flame's apocalyptic vision to burn the Erdtree and everything else to ash.
In the Frenzied Flame ending, Melina watches the destruction and vows to deliver the Tarnished's destined death.
The Age of Stars ending belongs to Ranni and requires completing her questline, becoming her champion and lord, and retrieving her ring.
In the Age of Stars ending, after the Elden Beast falls, Ranni's summon sign appears offering the Tarnished a choice instead of Marika's fractured form.
When summoned, Ranni appears in her true form as an enormous, radiant, divine being who replaces Marika in the world's structure, with the Dark Moon becoming the new guiding light.
Ranni tells the Tarnished she will give birth to a new and fleeting world and calls the Tarnished her consort, and together they leave the Lands Between on a thousand-year voyage into the stars.
In the Age of Stars ending, the world below begins its first night without the golden light that has governed it since before living memory.
Ranni describes her intended Age of Stars as one of unalloyed cold darkness, a thousand-year voyage into darkness guided by the Dark Moon.
In Ranni's envisioned age, the Erdtree would no longer be the center of power, the golden economy of souls would be disrupted, and mortal natural death would be restored in some form.
Whether Ranni's Age of Stars ending is truly good for the people of the Lands Between is left ambiguous by the game.
St. Trina urges the player to kill Miquella to grant him forgiveness for the tragedy his divinity would bring.
Under the Golden Order, ordinary people did not truly die; their spirits returned to the Erdtree through underground catacombs to be sustained or sent back.
Demigods and lords under the Golden Order could be killed in battle but could not permanently die, due to the removal of the Rune of Death.
The Tarnished receives a call in the form of a golden guiding thread of grace that leads toward the Erdtree, promising the chance to restore the Elden Ring and become Elden Lord.
The fight against Fortissax is accessed through Fia's questline in the deathbed dream, retrieving the Cursemark of Death.
The in-game Radahn Festival event allows players to summon multiple NPC allies, such as Blaidd and Alexander, representing his soldiers' way of honoring him with a worthy final battle.
In her boss fight, Malenia heals from every hit she lands on the player, even through guard, draining the player's vitality and reflecting her lifelong survival philosophy of aggression as defense.
The fight against Placidusax is accessed by lying down among ancient bones arranged in a circle as a ritual invitation.
Defeating Maliketh releases the Rune of Death back into the world, allowing destined death to return and making the previously golden-thorn-sealed Erdtree penetrable for the final stages of the game.
Grace can call to Tarnished descendants generations later even if they have no direct memory of the original promise, drawing them back to the Lands Between.
Sorcery in Elden Ring's mythology draws power from glintstone, crystallized cosmic starlight, making it a source of power independent of the Erdtree.
The Mimic Tear takes on the player character's appearance, weapons, armor, and spells, fighting as an exact copy of the player without their consciousness or history.
The fog gate is interpreted as a threshold of attention, separating the ordinary world from a story the game has been saving, requiring commitment to enter and encounter it fully.
Crucible-referencing incantations let the caster temporarily manifest animalistic traits such as tails, wings, or armored carapaces, echoing the primordial blending of life.
Tarnished who die can be revived repeatedly by the grace that resurrects them, allowing effectively unlimited deaths and returns.
The game describes the power of the Great Runes as a 'mad taint' rather than a pure gift, amplifying each demigod's existing traits.
The grace light from the Erdtree now appears only as thin, faint Sites of Grace guiding tarnished, remnants of a nearly depleted divine power.
Malenia can bloom a smaller version of the Scarlet Aeonia during battle, filling the arena with rot.
The Tarnished consumes Great Runes taken from fallen demigods over the course of the journey.
The Sites of Grace are depicted narratively as fragments of the Erdtree's fading grace and the world's memory of what it was meant to be.
Each Site of Grace points in a direction suggesting where the player should go next, but players can choose to ignore this guidance and explore elsewhere.
It is implied that warrior jars absorb the essence and martial prowess of the fallen warriors they consume.
Before being granted an audience with Rykard and joining the family, newly recruited Tarnished must invade fellow Tarnished to prove their resolve.
Leda urges the player to touch the withered arm, a portal to the Realm of Shadow where Miquella resides.
Dryleaf Dane's fighting style, Dane's Footwork, emphasizes powerful and precise kicks developed through training under a waterfall.
The Shadow of the Erdtree DLC added a full set of new bosses set in the Land of Shadow, a hidden realm tied to Miquella's great migration and ancient Golden Order history.
Elden Ring sold over 25 million copies.
The mythology of Elden Ring was created by George R. R. Martin, while the narrative and worldbuilding were developed by Hidetaka Miyazaki and FromSoftware.

In cut content, Kale would have discovered his people, the Great Caravan, were falsely accused of worshipping the Three Fingers and summoning the frenzied flame, filling him with spite toward the Greater Will and Golden Order.
FromSoftware has stated that Elden Ring is an independent title with its own storyline, though some fans theorize it may connect to the Dark Souls series as a prequel.
Hewg the Blacksmith was assigned by Queen Marika to forge a weapon capable of slaying God but was unable to complete it in time, as stated in his dialogue.
Some of the most important discoveries in the Lands Between, such as underground cities, hidden questlines, and optional bosses, are not indicated by the Sites of Grace guidance.

Fan theories propose that the puppets found in the hidden basement behind Caria Manor, including a Nox, an Omenkiller, Dolores the Sleeping Arrow, Finger Maiden Therolina, a Jarwright, and a hidden Sellen puppet, may all belong to Seluvis.
Theories suggest the Omenkiller puppet may have been meant to frame Gideon Ofnir for the slaughter in the Albinauric village, disillusioning Nephali.
Marika's exile of Godfrey was part of a larger plan to forge warriors through hardship outside the Erdtree's grace, creating the Tarnished.
In truth, Miquella orchestrated his own kidnapping, having charmed Mohg to gain access to the Realm of Shadow through Mohg's blood rituals.
Nokron the Eternal City is theorized to have succeeded in creating the god-slaying weapon Marika sought, but was accused of treason and destroyed, its remnants banished underground.

It is implied Marika came to understand that the Greater Will was indifferent rather than benevolent, and that the Golden Order's gift of immortality was actually a means of recycling souls to feed the Erdtree.

Marika began to harbor doubts about the Greater Will and the Golden Order, and is speculated to have had a hand in the Night of the Black Knives due to rumored connections with the Black Knife Assassins.
Rykard had a hand in the Night of the Black Knives, though to an unclear extent.

One theory holds that Marika did not shatter the Elden Ring purely out of rage over Godwyn's death, but that his death partially restored her sanity enough to break the Ring in an attempt to find the strongest champion to become Elden Lord or free her from suffering.
A theory suggests Marika created Melina and gave her the mission to burn down the Erdtree, and Melina wandered the Lands Between searching for her purpose.
The theory continues that the resulting war of the demigods ended without a clear winner, as Radahn and Malenia proved equal in strength.

The theory further suggests Marika used her last shimmer of grace to invite even Tarnished to compete for the Great Runes and become Elden Lord, granting them revival upon death, while Radagon tries to hinder this plan using the Erdtree's roots.

Radagon represents the male identity devoted to repairing the Elden Ring, while Marika as her female identity is the one who shattered it; the same being works simultaneously to destroy and repair the Elden Ring.
The Elden Beast is constitutively connected to the Elden Ring, acting as its guardian not by choice but because it and the Ring are the same kind of cosmic instrument of the Greater Will.
The Elden Beast attacks the player automatically as an expression of enforcing cosmic order, not out of personal malice.
The existence of two identical Astels suggests either multiple meteor arrivals of such beings or that Astel can replicate itself in ways defying normal biology.
Fighting the Mimic Tear is interpreted as a fight against one's own reflection, raising questions about identity and selfhood without the game commenting on it directly.
Trolls' aggression toward the player is interpreted as the defensive response of beings long accustomed to dangerous labor, rather than the behavior of guardians or dedicated enemies.
Demi-Humans are treated as animals by Golden Order society despite having their own organized communities and genuine queens who command real loyalty.
The scarlet rot treats growth and decay as phases of a single process, collapsing the Golden Order's strict binary between life and death.
Crumbling Farum Azula exists outside normal time, which is interpreted as the reason these ancient Crucible beings have been preserved there intact.
The appearance of Bell Bearing Hunters implies that something violent is happening to the merchants themselves, though the game never fully explains the connection.
The nature of Relena's connection to Rennala (student, contemporary, relative, or otherwise) is never definitively established by the game.
Gaius embodies institutional loyalty so complete that questioning the chain of command is not a cognitive option for him.
Romina is described as a saint who has achieved complete identification with the cosmic principle of rot she serves, such that the rot is not something she has but something she is.
Every boss in Elden Ring has an underlying story explaining why they are what they are and why they are found where they are, rather than being simple monsters.

Most bosses were engaged in their own ongoing existence before the player's arrival: Radahn was holding back the stars, Rennala was singing to her amber egg, Fortissax was fighting deathblight in the roots, the Fire Giant was chained to his forge, and Placidusax was waiting.
Elden Ring's bosses are framed as arguments the game makes about what power costs and what devotion produces, rather than mere obstacles.
Godrick represents the argument that borrowed power is still power, but remains borrowed.
Rennala represents the argument that grief is its own kind of kingdom.
Radagon represents the argument that a person can outlast everything that made them who they were.
Morgott represents the argument that one can love something that hates them, and that love can sustain without saving.
Malenia represents the argument that containing a god is its own form of power, and releasing it is honesty rather than defeat.
Power in the Lands Between is framed as the scar tissue of trauma: usually what remains after loss, what compensates for lack, or what was gained by surviving the unsurvivable.
Godrick is framed as what the Shattering produced in someone too weak to compete for the largest fragments of the Elden Ring.
Rennala is framed as what the Shattering produced in someone whose connection to the Elden Ring was given to her rather than inherited.
Radahn is framed as what the Shattering produced in someone strong enough to fight for a fragment of the Elden Ring but too damaged to use it.
Morgott is framed as what the Shattering produced in someone who never held a fragment of the Elden Ring but devoted himself to the memory of its wholeness.
Malenia is framed as what the Shattering produced in someone whose fragment of the Elden Ring was always inside her, inseparable from her suffering.
The Tarnished is given purpose by the Shattering as someone with nothing left to lose, able to seek the truth of the Lands Between that no other being already present could uncover.
Ranni sought to follow the Dark Moon, a distant cosmic force offering freedom rather than order, instead of the Erdtree's Golden Order.
The Greater Will is not the only cosmic power in Elden Ring's theology; it dominates the current age through the Erdtree and Marika's godhood while other Outer Gods contest for influence.
If the Scarlet Aeonia blooms three times, Malenia will become a true goddess and complete vessel for the rot; she has bloomed once so far.
Frenzied Flame theology holds that the Greater Will erred by creating individuals, and that all suffering should be melted back into unified oneness.
Fia has devoted herself to restoring natural death in a world that forcibly removes it, loving the Prince of Death despite its inability to love her back.
The Lands Between is not a world waiting to be saved but one already broken in ways a single Tarnished cannot simply fix by fighting to the top.
Many demigods the Tarnished fights became monstrous not from birth but because the world, their great runes, or prolonged grief shaped them that way.
Melina is characterized as the first genuinely kind presence the Tarnished encounters in the Lands Between.
All six Elden Ring endings involve continuing something—a cycle, a new order, a destruction, or a departure—rather than providing a clean, final resolution.
Elden Ring's narrative explores themes of inherited systems and structures that claim authority based on an origin story the player never witnessed.
The Erdtree is characterized as a parasitic structure whose golden light hides the fact that the Greater Will is distant and alien.
The immortality offered by the Erdtree's cycle comes at the cost of souls being returned to feed the Greater Will's cosmic system.
None of the alternative powers challenging the Golden Order—Ranni's cold moon, Miquella's compassion, Goldmask's order, or the Frenzied Flame's destruction—are presented as clearly better solutions.
Some theorize Bernahl's maiden succumbed to the frenzied flame, while others theorize she was thrown into the Forge of the Giants as fuel to burn the Erdtree, similar to Melina.

It is speculated that the person who gathered two Great Runes before the Tarnished was either Bernahl, whose armor suggests he was worthy of becoming Lord, or Vyke, said to be the closest anyone came to becoming Elden Lord before turning to the Frenzied Flame.
There is speculation Radagon may be a smaller-sized Fire Giant, based on descriptions of the Sword of Milos and Giant's Red Braid.
Another theory holds that Radagon was cursed with red hair by the Fire Giants as a result of the Golden Order's war against them.
It is speculated that Golden Order Incantations require both Faith and Intelligence because Radagon learned sorceries as Rennala's consort and incantations as Marika's consort.
It is unclear whether Marika and Radagon were always one being, whether Radagon is a fragment of Marika, or whether they became one after becoming consorts, as Melina's dialogue suggests.
Community lore theories debate whether the Lands Between's timeline is linear or cyclical, with multiple Erdtrees possibly rising after prior ages ruled by Giants, Dragons, or Tarnished.
One theory suggests the Elden Ring might be a symbolic measure of power, an artifact controlled by the Elden Lord, or a form assumed by the Elden Beast to fulfill the Greater Will's goals.
One theory suggests Marika shattered the Elden Ring to drive Godfrey out of the Lands Between and initiate the Long March of the Tarnished.

Fan theories debate whether Marika is a fixed entity vested with godhood by the Greater Will, or a specific being who arrived from the lands of the Numen in a manner similar to the Tarnished's recall.
Some theorize that Radagon and Marika's relationship mirrors the duality of Miquella and St. Trina, both being two aspects of one being.
Fan theory suggests the Erdtree may simply be the Greater Will's method of diverting the souls of the dead to harvest life-force and dominate death itself through the Golden Order.
A community theory suggests the Nox may have initiated the Night of the Black Knives as a plot possibly connected to Ranni, though her exact role (mastermind or ritual performer) is debated.
Count Ymir reveals disillusionment with the Erdtree and Marika, lamenting the world's inherent flaws and humanity's inability to find redemption.
St. Trina expresses concern that Miquella's ascension to godhood would be a curse rather than a blessing, trapping him beyond saving.

events.summary: In the primordial Crucible age, all life existed in chaotic communion without species divisions, centered on an older Great Tree, and ancient dragons may have followed their own prior cosmic order.
Giants worshipped the primitive Fell God and tended a ruinous flame; the Nox built underground cities of artificial stars; the Elden Beast's essence existed as the living Elden Ring.

The Greater Will sent its daughter Marika, a Numen, along with the golden Elden Beast, to the Lands Between, where she became a god at the Gate of Divinity and founded the Golden Order, and the Erdtree grew over and subsumed the older Great Tree.

The Nox and other peoples (the eternal cities' scholars) rebelled against the Greater Will and were punished by having their civilizations exiled underground; the Scadutree Avatar's guardianship and the Land of Shadow predate the Erdtree's dominance.

Under the new order, former Crucible traits like horns and wings became marks of shame; Omens and the Misbegotten were enslaved, while ancient Crucible Knights and the Night's Cavalry persisted from the earlier age.

Marika chose the warlord Hoarah Loux (Godfrey) as her first consort; wearing the Beast Regent Serosh to quell his bloodlust, he became the first Elden Lord and led wars expanding the Golden Order, fighting dragons, the Storm Lord, and the Academy's Carian royalty.

Marika and Godfrey waged a devastating war against the Fire Giants and the Fell God, nearly annihilating them, though one giant was deliberately spared and chained to tend the forge flame at the Mountaintops of the Giants.

With no more wars to fight, Marika stripped Godfrey and his warriors of their grace and exiled them as the first Tarnished in the Long March, promising their grace would one day be restored so they could return and compete to become Elden Lord.

Godfrey and Marika's children included Godwyn the Golden and the Omen twins Morgott and Mohg, who were hidden and shackled beneath Leyndell for their Crucible-like deformities; Maliketh was given to Marika as her Shadow to guard the Rune of Death.

Rennala, a gifted astrologer who learned lunar magic, became Queen of the Full Moon and head of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, marrying Radagon after their forces clashed in the Liurnian Wars, uniting Leyndell and the Academy.

Radagon and Rennala had three children—Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni—before Radagon abandoned the family, gifting Rennala an amber egg, to rejoin Marika as her consort, leaving Rennala devastated and the Academy's scholars in rebellion against the Carian family.

Messmer was sent to purge the Hornsent, an older religion's people whom the Golden Order deemed Omens, decimating them and later being erased from official history and sent to conquer the Land of Shadow.

Under the Golden Order, mortals' souls returned to the Erdtree instead of truly dying, and demigods could not permanently die, while Marika privately began doubting the Greater Will's benevolence, suspecting the immortality cycle merely recycled souls to feed the Erdtree.

Ranni, destined to become an Empyrean candidate controlled by the Two Fingers, rejected this fate; she and her brother Radahn each sought ways to escape or control destiny, Radahn locking the stars in place with gravity magic to stop her plan.

Ranni orchestrated the Night of the Black Knives: Black Knife Assassins, Numen women under her sway, stole a fragment of the Rune of Death from Maliketh and used it to kill Godwyn the Golden's soul while his body lived on, and Ranni died in the flesh at the same moment to free her soul into a doll body, escaping the Two Fingers' control.

Godwyn's soulless body festered within the Erdtree's roots, becoming the corrupting Prince of Death, while the dragon Fortissax, his loyal companion, descended to fight the spreading deathblight in an endless, unwinnable battle.

Devastated by Godwyn's murder, Marika shattered the Elden Ring, breaking reality's fundamental laws and imprisoning herself, while Radagon (her other self) tried to repair it with the same hammer; this ignited the Shattering, a war among the demigods over the Ring's scattered shards.
Maliketh bound the Rune of Death within his own body and changed his name to prevent it being stolen again, while Marika's grief also drove her to create (or empower) Melina with a hidden purpose.

During the Shattering, Malenia's Cleanrot Knights clashed with Radahn's army at the bloody Battle of Aeonia; her needle broke, unleashing the Scarlet Bloom that devastated Caelid, and both combatants fell—Malenia into a coma, Radahn's mind destroyed by rot though his body survived.

A loyal knight, Finlay, carried the comatose Malenia back to the Haligtree, the sanctuary Miquella had grown from a sapling watered with his own blood, where scarlet rot continued to spread despite his hopes of a pure refuge.

While Malenia fought Radahn, Mohg kidnapped the sleeping Miquella, wrapping him in a cocoon of blood and silk in a secret ritual meant to elevate him to godhood and make Mohg his consort; unknown to Mohg, Miquella had engineered his own capture to access the Land of Shadow.

Rykard offered himself to the God-Devouring Serpent, merging with it to become immortal and turning Volcano Manor into a haven for recusants rejecting the Golden Order, though his fall into gluttony drove away most followers save for his consort Tanith.

With no faction able to achieve decisive victory, the Shattering settled into a stalemate: Leyndell stood leaderless with Morgott secretly ruling in disguise, and the Greater Will fell silent, abandoning the Lands Between.

In the aftermath, Vyke sacrificed himself to the Frenzied Flame to save his finger maiden but became a mad Lord of Frenzy, losing his chance at the throne; other claimants like Godrick the Grafted (weakest of Godfrey's line) built grotesque power through grafting conquered limbs.

Mohg escaped the Shunning-Grounds to found Mohgwyn Palace, a blood-soaked dynasty devoted to the Formless Mother who had granted him bloodflame power after his crucible-marked blood caught fire before her.

Years later, grace calls new generations of Tarnished, including the player's character, back to the Lands Between to seek the shattered Great Runes and become Elden Lord, guided by the mysterious Melina.

The Tarnished's journey leads through demigod-held territories: Limgrave and Stormveil Castle, where Morgott (disguised as Margit) tests the Tarnished before revealing himself as the castle's true guardian and later the Erdtree's most devoted defender.

The Tarnished defeats Godrick the Grafted in Stormveil, ending his grotesque rule, after which Kenneth Haight and Gatekeeper Gostoc help install Nepheli Loux, Godfrey's adopted heir, as the new ruler of Limgrave.

In Liurnia, the Tarnished encounters the Carian royal family's remnants, including Ranni (now in a doll body) and her retinue Blaidd, Iji, and Seluvis, as she continues her covert scheme to usurp the Two Fingers and bring about an Age of Stars.
The Tarnished defeats Rennala, breaking her grief-stricken hold over the ruined Academy, where she still clutches Radagon's amber egg and sings to her loyal students.

Elsewhere, Rykard's Volcano Manor recruits recusant Tarnished to assassinate rivals, maintained by figures like Tanith, Patches, Bernahl, and the disguised serpent-woman Rya (Zorayas), while followers like Rogier and the Dung Eater pursue their own dark obsessions with Those Who Live in Death.

General Radahn's loyal soldiers, unable to kill their beloved but rot-ravaged general, hold the Radahn Festival so he can die in honorable battle; his defeat shakes a star loose from the sky, opening the buried city of Nokron, which Ranni needed for her plan.
In Nokron, the Tarnished retrieves the Finger-Slayer Blade and other relics from the Nox's rebellious legacy, aiding Ranni's search for the Dark Moon Ring at the Moonlight Altar.

The Tarnished explores deeper realms and confronts ancient powers: the dormant Dragonlord Placidusax in the time-locked ruins of Farum Azula, and the chained, legless Fire Giant maintaining the forge flame at the Mountaintops of the Giants.

The Tarnished journeys to Caelid and the Haligtree, eventually awakening the long-sleeping Malenia, who still waits for Miquella's return and fights with a rot-fueled, life-draining ferocity before being defeated.

The Tarnished confronts Mohg at his blood-soaked palace, preventing his plan to use the captive Miquella for his own ascension, while nearby the loyal fanatic White Mask Varre continues to serve the Mohgwyn Dynasty even in defeat.

Maliketh, the Black Blade and betrayed warrior once called 'Death of the Demigods,' is defeated, releasing the Rune of Death back into the world and finally breaking the golden thorns sealing the Erdtree.

Melina, revealing her true purpose, sacrifices herself at the Forge of the Giants as kindling to burn open the Erdtree so the Tarnished may enter it—unless the Tarnished has already taken the Frenzied Flame, in which case she instead vows to deliver their destined death.

Inside Leyndell, Godfrey's ghost confronts the Tarnished and, upon the Erdtree's thorns falling, returns in full as Hoarah Loux, tearing off the spirit Serosh to fight in his unrestrained, primal berserker form.

Deep within the Erdtree, the Tarnished confronts Radagon, Marika's devoted other half who tried in vain to repair the shattered Ring, and upon his defeat he transforms into Marika and then releases the Elden Beast, the Greater Will's cosmic enforcer of Order.
After the Elden Beast falls, the shattered Elden Ring and the fractured, silent Marika await the Tarnished's final choice, which will determine the fate of the Lands Between.

Depending on the Tarnished's path, one of several endings unfolds: mending the Ring plainly as Elden Lord, establishing Goldmask's transcendent Age of Order, restoring natural death through Fia's Age of Duskyn, embracing the Dung Eater's nihilistic Blessing of Despair, becoming the Frenzied Flame's apocalyptic Lord of Chaos, or joining Ranni to usher in the cold, star-guided Age of Stars as her consort.

Separately, in the Land of Shadow (explored via the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion), Miquella's true ambition is revealed: to become a god of compassion free of the Greater Will by capturing Radahn's soul and placing it in Mohg's body, having manipulated loyal followers—Leda, Freyja, Ansbach, Thiollier, the Hornsent, and others—through his supernatural charm.
